title: Introduction to Broadcasting
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose of introduction to broadcasting and name one situation where it is useful.
Apply meaning of broadcasting to a small NumPy example and inspect the resulting values, shape, or dtype.
Identify one important limitation, boundary case, or validation check for introduction to broadcasting.

content.intro: This lesson develops topic 78 of the supplied curriculum: **Introduction to Broadcasting**. The main starting point is **Meaning of broadcasting**. You will connect the idea to a small, synthetic example, then use the result to reason about shape, dtype, accuracy, or memory as appropriate.
content.why_it_matters: Broadcasting allows compatible shapes to operate without explicitly copying repeated values. Reason about the dimensions from the rightmost side before changing the arrays.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Treat **Introduction to Broadcasting** as an explicit step in an array workflow. This lesson centers on **Meaning of broadcasting** and the source syllabus's related subtopics. Before trusting a result, identify the input shape and dtype, perform the smallest useful operation, and inspect the output. The example uses synthetic data so you can change one value and observe what changes.

content_blocks.code:
import numpy as np

prices = np.array([10, 20, 30])
print(prices + 5)

common_mistakes.why: Broadcasting compares dimensions from the right.
common_mistakes.fix: Write the shapes side by side and align their rightmost dimensions.

common_mistakes.why: Explicit tiling can allocate extra memory.
common_mistakes.fix: Try broadcasting with singleton dimensions first.
